claims.statement: Scope-only record. No scanner layer or adapter exists for Starlette: the catalog entry is a registration, not support, and nothing is claimed as extracted. The must-catch entries and their oracle baselines are what a future scanner must produce or leave unknown. No support statement may be issued from this record.

runtime_tested.reason: Runtime-tested needs a request-level verifier (T16 / beval in the audit plan) that serves requests against a pinned install; none was run. This package only read the framework route table at import time, so every runtime or request claim stays BLOCKED.

must_catch.construct: Route(path, endpoint, methods=[...]) with a typed path parameter and a Mount("/api", routes=[...]) in Starlette(routes=[...]) (the baseline a future scanner must extract)
Route objects built by a comprehension over a name list with an endpoint factory
Mount("/static", app=StaticFiles(...)): a mount of a framework-provided ASGI app; the route table shows only the prefix and no methods
uvicorn root_path="/svc" passed at server start, outside the application object

conformance.reason: No Starlette scanner layer or adapter exists: adapters/http-wave-bc/catalog.mjs only admits the target (id python-starlette) and the static runner has no layer for it, so there is no static output to compare. Only oracle baselines are stored; the comparison is BLOCKED until an extraction layer exists.

oracle_range.kind: Framework route table read at import time through public framework APIs, in a venv holding exactly the pinned wheel(s). oracle.py shares no code with the scanners and never serves a request.
can_verify: which paths and methods the framework registers after importing the fixture (non-generated pairs)
which routes the framework generates itself (docs, openapi, static, admin) and their paths
prefix composition, mounts and include flattening exactly as the framework computes them
trailing-slash and converter spelling of the registered path
cannot_verify: request handling: middleware execution, authentication outcomes, redirects, status codes or response bodies
deployment prefix behaviour (root_path, APPLICATION_ROOT, FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME, reverse-proxy rewriting)
any framework version or Python version other than the pinned ones
routes registered after import (at request time) or by code the fixture does not execute

executed_commands.stdout_unstored: PyPI JSON API response at fetch time (volatile registry state); results/registry.json keeps the fields this record relies on

limits: Route-set evidence only: the oracle is the framework route table read at import time. Nothing in this record issued an HTTP request, so no entry is Runtime-tested.

HEAD and OPTIONS are dropped from the stored expected pairs. A method the framework does not report is stored as "-"; a future scanner pair with a null method compares as "-" and counts as unresolved, never as an exact match.

CI does not reinstall the framework: the stored oracle output is bound by sha256, by the pin and by the sha256 of oracle.py. There is no scanner to re-run; the verifier fails when a scanner or adapter file named after the framework appears (adapter-appeared), so this record cannot outlive a new adapter unnoticed.
Only the pinned version was run. Releases uploaded after the pinned wheel are listed per package and are not covered.

record_digest seals the whole record, so an edit that is not re-sealed fails. Prose is sealed, not recomputed: statement, reasons, limits, plan, oracle_range text, layer roles, construct and covers texts are not derived from evidence, so a re-sealed prose edit is not detected by the verifier and must be caught in review.
Mount of a non-route ASGI app (StaticFiles) appears in the oracle as a row with methods unknown (method "-"); a future scanner must keep it as unknown-method instead of inventing methods.
plan: HTTP-python-starlette-02 (not started): T06 needs Route/Mount/decorator facts and a T13 adapter before any static comparison; the expected pairs stored per must-catch entry are the acceptance baseline. Until then the target stays unsupported.
